page: Amazon Web Services m6a.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at up to 3.6 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with hyperthreading. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware integrates standard cryptographic and vector extensions such as AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and AVX, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX instructions. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps. This instance type contains no bundled local storage and includes zero dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark results place the m6a.16xlarge in the top 25 percent for multi-threaded and compute-dense evaluations. Its multi-core capability is confirmed by high scores in PassMark CPU (67,467.01) and Stress-NG multi-core (95,666.41), alongside strong code compilation throughput in Clang (42,573.0) and ray tracing (69,625.0). Cached memory bandwidth reaches 4,518.65 GB/sec, supporting fast in-memory transactions evidenced by 67.36 million Redis SET operations per second and a strong PassMark database operations metric of 26,727.95. Conversely, large uncached block reads (123.14 GB/sec) and writes (62.54 GB/sec) fall into the middle 50 percent, as do single-core Geekbench results (1,675.0) and static web serving throughput (34.24 GB/sec).

From an efficiency perspective, the AMD EPYC platform offers high multi-threaded density per core at general-purpose allocation levels. While lacking local NVMe disk access or hardware matrix acceleration limits its utility for high-throughput local disk caching and heavy generative AI serving, its massive core footprint and strong memory caching yield efficient horizontal scaling. The m6a.16xlarge is primarily suited for large multi-threaded application servers, distributed database nodes, Redis caching layers, enterprise backend services, and CI/CD compilation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor, featuring a 64-vCPU AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz across 32 physical cores, coupled with 256.0 GB of DDR4 RAM. Operating with a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, it delivers 25 Gbps baseline networking, without local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-core compute capability, with top-tier performance across Stress-NG multi-core, PassMark CPU, Clang compilation, and in-memory key-value workloads executing over 67 million Redis SET operations per second. Single-core speeds and uncached memory bandwidth show average throughput. With robust multi-threaded processing and substantial DDR4 capacity, m6a.16xlarge is engineered for demanding multi-threaded enterprise applications, in-memory caches, large database nodes, CI/CD build servers, and backend services.
